notes.title: How the cuisine filters were policed
notes.body: Every food card names a specific dish — a cuisine label alone doesn’t qualify. Columbus’s signature strength is range: Jeni’s Splendid ice cream (born here), the North Market, Columbus-style square-cut pizza, Schmidt’s German sausage & cream puffs, and one of the largest Somali tables in the US, sourced to the Columbus Dispatch, Columbus Monthly and Columbus Underground. A cuisine tag names the kitchen’s own tradition, never one dish it happens to serve.

notes.title: Web-searched and fact-checked
notes.body: Every place is traceable to a credible source — Michelin, Eater SF, The Infatuation, SF Chronicle, Mercury News, Atlas Obscura and official sites — recorded in data/sources.json (direct map/page fetches are blocked in the build environment, so sources were confirmed via search). Every coordinate is verified into data/geocodes.json and every place status-checked open.

places.w: Ohio's 1861 Greek Revival capitol on Capitol Square — free tours, the Statehouse Museum, and grounds dotted with monuments in the heart of downtown.

places.n: Franklin Park Conservatory and Botanical Gardens
places.w: An 1895 glasshouse built for a world's fair, with themed biomes, a permanent Chihuly glass collection and blooming seasonal gardens on the near east side.
The Center of Science and Industry — a top-ranked U.S. science museum in an Arata Isozaki building on the Scioto riverfront, with giant hands-on exhibits and a dinosaur gallery.
Strong holdings of American and European modernism (including Columbus native George Bellows) in a 1931 Renaissance-revival building with a light-filled modern wing.
Ohio State's contemporary-art laboratory in Peter Eisenman's landmark 1989 Deconstructivist building — galleries, avant-garde film and performance at the campus's edge.

places.n: The Book Loft of German Village
places.w: A literary labyrinth of 32 rooms of discounted books in pre-Civil War buildings — one of the largest independent bookstores in the country.
The only park based on a painting: sculpted yews recreate Seurat's 'A Sunday on La Grande Jatte' — 54 people, boats and dogs — on the Old Deaf School Park grounds. Free.
The 1922 horseshoe-shaped, 100,000-plus-seat home of Buckeyes football — an enduring icon of college-football gameday and a National Register landmark.
Columbus's oldest park (donated 1851) in Victorian Village — a pond, fountain and gazebo, and host of the summer ComFest gathering.
A free 13-acre rose garden inside Clintonville's Whetstone Park — 11,000-plus roses across 350-plus varieties, at their peak in June.
One of America's premier zoos (Jack Hanna's longtime home base), north of the city in Powell, with the Zoombezi Bay water park next door.
Downtown's riverfront promenade — a 15,000-sq-ft interactive fountain, gardens and skyline views stretching along the Scioto from the Arena District to the Whittier Peninsula.
The 1927 Art Deco skyscraper that has defined the skyline for a century — 555 feet, now a hotel, lit in changing colors nightly.

places.n: Grange Insurance Audubon Center and Scioto Audubon Metro Park
places.w: A LEED-Platinum birding center on the restored Whittier Peninsula wetlands, plus a 35-ft outdoor climbing wall and downtown skyline views. Free.
Columbus's last true public market (est. 1876) — 30-plus merchants including the original Jeni's, Momo Ghar and Hoyo's, just off the Short North and Arena District.

places.ad: N High St (Goodale St to W 5th Ave), Columbus, OH 43215
places.w: The gallery, restaurant and shopping spine on High Street between downtown and OSU, marked by its signature lit metal arches; monthly Gallery Hop has run since 1984.
The restored home of humorist and New Yorker cartoonist James Thurber, now a literary center, museum and bookstore on a Jefferson Avenue historic row.

A 19th-century German immigrant neighborhood of brick-paved streets and Italianate cottages — the largest privately funded historic district on the National Register. Address is the German Village Society Meeting Haus.
The 11-acre historic green at the heart of OSU's campus, framed by University Hall and Thompson Library and landscaped with Olmsted-brothers input — the campus 'living room.'

A 13-plus-mile paved riverside greenway from downtown's North Bank Park up through OSU and Clintonville to Worthington — the city's spine for cycling and running. Address is the southern North Bank Park trailhead.

The historic district just east of the Short North — brick worker cottages and the redeveloped Jeffrey Park, now home to Seventh Son and Fox in the Snow. Address is the landmark Jeffrey Manufacturing office building.

places.n: Ohio History Center and Ohio Village
places.w: The state history museum in a striking 1970 Brutalist building, with the adjacent Ohio Village recreating an 1890s town. Ohio Village is under phased restoration into the mid-2020s.

The only congressionally designated national museum for veterans of every branch and era, in a sculptural 2018 concrete-arch building (Allied Works) on the Scioto's west bank, ringed by a memorial grove and rooftop sanctuary.
A restored 1908 downtown engine house of hand-drawn, horse-drawn and early motorized fire apparatus, with a kids' play space and fire-safety tours.

places.n: Columbus Museum of Art at The Pizzuti
places.w: CMA's contemporary satellite in a restored Short North building — rotating exhibitions drawn from Ron and Ann Pizzuti's globe-spanning collection of contemporary art.

German Village's 23-acre green heart (est. 1867) — Columbus's second-oldest park, with a lake, the Umbrella Girl fountain, a bust of poet Friedrich Schiller and summer 'Actors' Theatre' Shakespeare. Free.
The world's largest collection of cartoons and comics — original Calvin and Hobbes, Peanuts and Pogo art — in Ohio State's Sullivant Hall, with free rotating gallery exhibitions.
A 24,000-sq-ft shrine to the Golden Bear — the Columbus-born golf legend — inside the OSU sports complex, tracing his record 18 major championships.

Ohio State's free natural-history gem inside the 1893 Romanesque Orton Hall (a National Historic Landmark built of Ohio stone) — a full Cretodus shark, a giant ground sloth and thousands of fossils and minerals.
A 60-plus-acre living plant collection across OSU's campus — ornamental Learning Gardens, a conifer and hosta collection and a Chartres-style labyrinth. Open dawn to dusk, free.
An 1852 Greek Revival/Italianate home on the near east side, a documented Underground Railroad stop, preserved with original Kelton-family furnishings and a period garden.
A 1905 brick mansion built by Columbus mayor Robert H. Jeffrey, willed to Bexley in 1941 and now the centerpiece of a 40-acre park of woodland trails, an Alum Creek overlook and a pool.

Central Ohio's home for independent and international film — a 1937 Art Deco/Art Moderne neighborhood movie house in Bexley, on the National Register and running continuously since Christmas Day 1937.

Ohio's second-largest cemetery (est. 1848) — a 325-acre garden cemetery and registered arboretum with an old-growth oak forest, ornate mausoleums and an Audubon Important Bird Area; resting place of the Wright brothers' family and Eddie Rickenbacker.
A National Cemetery on the Hilltop holding 2,200-plus Confederate soldiers who died at the Union's Camp Chase prison — rows of white headstones behind a boulder arch reading 'Americans.' Free.

places.w: A 7,000-plus-acre metro park on the state-and-national scenic Big and Little Darby Creeks — restored tallgrass prairie with a free-roaming bison herd, a nature center and miles of trail. Free.
Malcolm Cochran's 1994 public artwork — 109 six-foot white concrete ears of corn standing in rows in a Dublin park, a tribute to farmer Sam Frantz and the area's agricultural roots. Free.

pv.src: Apple Maps coordinate= place pin (Wikipedia concurs 40.0850,-83.1233)

places.w: The world's longest single-tower S-shaped suspension bridge (760 ft, opened 2020) — a curving pedestrian span whose deck threads the keyhole of a 169-ft tower, linking Historic Dublin to Riverside Crossing Park. Free.
A wooded ravine steps from Historic Dublin with a multi-tier waterfall dropping into Indian Run — boardwalks, viewing decks and a short trail named for its Wyandot campsite history. Free.
A 1,200-acre metro park north of the city named for its 100-ft shale bluffs over the Olentangy River — ten trails, a nature center, a sledding hill and ancient Adena burial mounds. Free.

pv.src: Apple Maps coordinate= place pin (visitor entrance/nature center)

places.w: A 123-acre metro park of themed display gardens in Westerville — herb, rose and woodland gardens, a Sisters' Garden and boardwalk nature trails through nature preserve. Free.

places.n: AMA Motorcycle Hall of Fame Museum
places.w: The American Motorcyclist Association's national museum in Pickerington — vintage and racing motorcycles and the Hall of Fame honoring the sport's legends.
A storybook 1925 Tudor Gothic library and cultural center in tiny Lithopolis, gifted by Mabel Wagnalls (of Funk & Wagnalls) in memory of her parents — stone, stained glass and a theater.
One of Worthington's oldest homes — an 1811 pioneer house with an 1816 Federal addition, restored by the Worthington Historical Society to show early-19th-century village life.

The 1850s Westerville home of the Hanby family — Bishop William Hanby, an Underground Railroad conductor and Otterbein co-founder, and son Benjamin, composer of 'Up on the Housetop' and abolitionist ballad 'Darling Nelly Gray.'

pv.src: HMdb Hanby House marker coordinate (40°7.585'N, 82°56.256'W), at Center St & W Main

places.w: The 'Official Theatre of the State of Ohio' — a lavishly gilded 1928 Spanish-Baroque movie palace on Capitol Square, saved from the wrecking ball in 1969 and declared a National Historic Landmark in 1977. CAPA runs it today, with free summer walking tours and 'Mighty Morton' organ demos.
places.k: Free guided tours on select summer Saturdays; otherwise a ticketed performance venue.

places.w: The oldest surviving theatre in central Ohio — opened 1896 as the 'Great Southern Fireproof Hotel and Opera House' after a run of downtown theatre fires, it hosted Sarah Bernhardt, Anna Pavlova and John Philip Sousa. CAPA restored it in a 14-month, $10M rebuild reopening in 1998.
A six-acre downtown green built on the footprint of the old City Center mall — a restored 1914 carousel, free summer concerts, a Thursday farmers market and 200+ free events a year. Free.

places.n: Union Station Arch at McFerson Commons
places.ad: McFerson Commons, Nationwide Blvd, Arena District, Columbus, OH 43215
places.w: The last surviving arch of Columbus's demolished 1897 Union Station (a Daniel Burnham design), rescued during the 1976 wrecking and re-erected as the centerpiece of the 2.2-acre McFerson Commons in the Arena District. Free.

The flagship of a system twice named National Library of the Year — its $30M 2016 daylight-flooded renovation (GUND Partnership), opening onto Topiary Park, won the Columbus Landmarks James B. Recchie Design Award. Free to wander.

places.w: Clintonville's beloved neighborhood movie house — opened 1938 as the Indianola Theatre, it's Columbus's oldest cinema and the last independent one left, famous as the first U.S. theater licensed to serve alcohol. Two screens, 40 taps and an in-house pizza kitchen.

places.ad: Blackmore Library, 4th Fl, 2199 E Main St, Bexley, OH 43209
places.w: Capital University's free art museum on the top floor of its Bexley library — 3,000+ works spanning Rembrandt, Dürer, Goya, Renoir, Cassatt, Picasso, Chagall and Warhol, plus rotating exhibits of Indigenous and local artists.
places.k: Free; open during the academic year only (closed summers and university holidays).

pv.src: Yelp/maps decimal place coords for Capital University campus

places.w: A 60,000-sq-ft Franklinton makerspace billed as the physically largest in the world — welding, blacksmithing, woodshop, 3D printing and 80+ classes a month, with free RSVP evening tours and demonstrations.
places.k: Free evening tours by RSVP; workshops/membership ticketed.

places.w: A 6,000-sq-ft Hilliard oddity holding 150+ working sets — mechanical 1920s scanning-disc TVs, prewar and early-color receivers — one of the world's deepest early-television collections. Free (donations welcome), weekends only.

Inside the Westerville library, in the League's old printing-plant town — 'the dry capital of the world' — the nation's foremost temperance/Prohibition collection: propaganda, artifacts and the story of the Ohio-born movement that drove the 18th Amendment. Free.
places.k: Free; open library hours or by appointment.

places.w: A 761-acre Metro Park wrapping the 11-acre Schrock Lake and the Edward S. Thomas State Nature Preserve, with old-growth oak-hickory-beech woods and a 3.8-mile paved multipurpose loop. Free.
A 653-acre Metro Park whose 118-acre Walden Waterfowl Refuge and 11-acre Thoreau Lake draw hundreds of birds — 220+ species logged — viewed from two elevated shelters with spotting scopes. Free.

places.ad: 1375 State Route 674 N, Canal Winchester, OH 43110
places.w: An 1880s working farm inside Slate Run Metro Park — costumed staff tend heirloom pigs, geese, turkeys and Percheron horses and cook in an 1856 Gothic-revival farmhouse, recreating daily central-Ohio farm life. Free.
places.k: Free; seasonal hours (open Tue–Sun; closed some winter days).

places.w: A 35-foot ravine waterfall in Dublin, reached by a short wheelchair-accessible boardwalk and staircase in Columbus's two-acre Hayden Falls Nature Preserve — best after rain. Free, distinct from Dublin's Indian Run Falls.

pv.src: Google Maps place pin !3d40.0673126!4d-83.1101064 (Hayden Falls Park)

places.w: A 30-million-visitor-a-year open-air 'town' laid out like a 1950s Main Street — 250+ shops from Nordstrom to Louis Vuitton alongside restaurants, cinemas and free public events. Repeatedly named the top retail experience in America. A tourism draw in its own right.

pv.src: coordinatesfinder.com decimal coords for 160 Easton Town Center address

places.w: A landmark 1836-37 National Road stagecoach inn in tiny Lafayette, said to be second only to the Golden Lamb among Ohio's oldest continuously recognized taverns; it hosted six U.S. presidents. Documented by the Library of Congress HABS survey. Closed 2020, reopened Feb 2023 and still operating as a historic tavern you can walk into.

places.ad: 3225 Plain City-Georgesville Rd, West Jefferson, OH 43162
places.w: A 2,200-acre Metro Park straddling the Madison-Franklin line along Big Darby Creek (a state and national scenic river), with restored prairie, quarry-pond beaches and paddling, and prime birding. The Madison County side lies west of the creek. Distinct from Battelle Darby Creek downstream.

places.n: Jeni's Splendid Ice Creams — North Market
places.w: Jeni Britton Bauer launched Jeni's at the North Market in 2002; the grassy-buttermilk base and inventive flavors (Brambleberry Crisp, Brown Butter Almond Brittle) that turned a Columbus stall into a national brand.
Phenomenal Himalayan dumplings that put Columbus's huge Nepali-Bhutanese community on the map; the jhol momo swim in a spiced sesame broth. Featured on Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives.

The friendly gateway to Columbus's Somali food scene (one of the largest Somali communities in the US): tender suqaar, crisp sambusas and rice served the traditional way with a banana. 'Hoyo' means mother.
German Village institution since 1886 in a brick livery stable. The Bahama Mama smoked sausage was voted Columbus's official food; the world-famous jumbo cream puffs are the other reason to come.

Family-owned since 1942 and home of the Thurmanator, a monster double burger loaded with ham, bacon and three cheeses. TEMPORARILY CLOSED after an April 2026 electrical fire; owners have vowed to rebuild — call ahead before visiting.

pv.ss: Closed indefinitely after Apr 12 2026 electrical fire (Columbus Today news; Yelp 'Temp. Closed' Aug 2026)

places.w: A Bexley shrine since 1954: ultra-thin cracker crust, cash only, no alcohol, hand-written checks and folded paper 'tents' — Columbus-style pizza at its most austere and beloved.
Columbus's oldest Italian restaurant (est. 1929, 'Talk of the Town'), credited with serving the city's first pizza. Wood-paneled, red-sauce, old-world charm.

A Columbus original that launched at the North Market in 2014 and built a devoted following (and a social mission) around its Nashville hot chicken. All central-Ohio locations closed in September 2025 — kept here for the record.

pv.ss: Known-closed (flagged in input); former North Market stall no longer listed at North Market

places.w: Chef Josh Dalton's glass-kitchen tasting menu, reinvented every few months — repeatedly ranked Columbus's #1 restaurant since 2012.
The rare brewery that's also one of the city's best restaurants — award-winning beers (the coffee-and-vanilla Daybreak cream ale) alongside a serious downtown dining room.
Columbus's family chocolatier since 1952 and maker of the definitive Ohio buckeye — peanut-butter fudge dipped in chocolate. Free factory tours on the west side.
German Village's see-and-be-seen bistro since 1981 — steaks, seafood and one of the most beloved leafy patios in America.
One of Columbus's OG craft breweries (2013), a local institution in Italian Village with street-level and second-floor patios in a former auto garage.
Chef Avishar Barua — a James Beard 'Best Chef: Great Lakes' semifinalist — cooks inventive, Bangladeshi-inflected New American on the German Village edge; a recent Columbus Monthly #1.
Italian Village's scratch bakery and hand-poured-coffee darling since 2014; the gooey cinnamon roll and egg sandwich draw morning lines.

Long-running Morse Rd Vietnamese room (murals, plastic fruit trees) singled out by Columbus Underground for a super-crunchy grilled-chicken banh mi and picked as a reviewers' favorite on alt.eats.columbus (Columbus Food Adventures). Google ~4.4 with high volume.

Columbus' pioneering ramen shop (Bethel Centre), routinely called the best ramen in the city — and named best in Ohio by a national food guide. Columbus Monthly ran a First Look, and it's covered on alt.eats.columbus and by creator Breakfast With Nick. Yelp 587 reviews / Google high-rated.

University District specialist in Dongbei (Northeastern/Manchurian) Chinese cooking — a rare regional cuisine for the city, reviewed by Columbus Underground and Columbus Monthly ("Short Order") and written up by creator Breakfast With Nick. Google high-rated with real volume.

North Market's Northern Vietnamese stall from Khanh Le and his mother Lan Pham (a North Market staple since 2010; earlier known as Lac Viet) — a from-scratch pho broth simmered 24 hours and crisp, balanced banh mi.

places.w: Specialty roaster's showcase Short North bar with a pour-over station and small sample-roaster; works directly with small coffee farmers and cooperatives, and among the strongest in-city options for locally roasted single-origin beans.

places.w: Columbus's original micro-roaster and coffee house (founded 1988 in Grandview) — 60-plus small-batch coffees hand-selected from 20-plus countries, plus pastries and locally made desserts.

pv.src: Wikipedia Bank Block Building (1255-1293 Grandview Ave) approx — spans the block, not exact storefront

places.w: The original City Barbeque, founded in Columbus in 1999 in a former doughnut shop by a team that won the American Royal Invitational for best brisket — the recipe that grew a Columbus-born pit-BBQ chain.

pv.src: aggregator decimal place coords (2111 W Henderson Rd)

places.w: A genuine National Road landmark still serving dinner — built 1836–37 in Lafayette and reputed to be Ohio's second-oldest stagecoach inn, host to six U.S. presidents (subject of an Ohio Historical Marker and National Road travel histories). Known today for prime rib and home-cooked specials. Open Tue–Sat (active listings, Aug 2026). Merit is the landmark itself; food is honest tavern fare.

pv.src: HMDB historical marker coords 39°56.268'N 83°24.415'W (same building as Lafayette entry)

places.w: Chefs Matt Heaggans & Catie Randazzo's cult smash burger — Ohio beef, American cheese, pickles and special sauce. A James Beard Blended Burger Project entrant that graduated from pop-up to a beloved Clintonville brick-and-mortar next to Combustion Brewery.
